description: Compliance risk register for a slot game programme. Phase 3 of the advisory engagement (see steering/advisory-engagement.md section 1).
instructions: Every risk MUST have a named owner and a due date. A risk register without owners is a list of opinions.
Impact is defined by CONSEQUENCE TYPE, not by a generic high/medium/low feeling. Use the impactLevels definitions below.

Include the consultant-specific risk categories. Engineering teams reliably identify product risks and reliably miss regulatory-currency, unverified-assumption, transitive and single-point-of-dependency risks.

impactLevels.critical: Cannot obtain certification, or already live and must be withdrawn. May involve unlawful operation.
impactLevels.high: Certification rejected requiring design rework; fines; licence condition breach.
impactLevels.medium: Certification delay; re-submission required; additional documentation required.
impactLevels.low: Explanation or supplementary documentation required; no schedule impact.

register.title: Product specification built on a MEDIUM or UNVERIFIED regulatory value
register.description: Example: designing a Malta build to a 92% RTP floor that could not be confirmed and may in fact be 85%. See steering/jurisdiction-matrix.md section 1.7.
register.mitigation: Retrieve the primary instrument. Until then, treat the value as a named project risk with a verification task and owner, not as a settled requirement.

register.title: Target market framework is mid-replacement or recently changed
register.description: Known instances: Gibraltar (2012 RTOS vs Gambling Bill 2025 and 2026 subsidiary legislation), Isle of Man (Gambling (Amendment) 2026), Nevada (Regulation 14 effective 2026-02-26 changing ITL submission content), West Virginia (179 CSR 10 effective 2026-04-27), Curacao (LOK transition and wind-down rules), Brazil (STF RE 966.177 due 2026-08-05), UK (three RTS changes in 15 months).
register.mitigation: Establish a quarterly regulatory review. Track named instruments and effective dates. Re-check submission packages prepared before a change date.

register.title: GLI and iTech Labs are the same corporate group
register.description: GLI acquired iTech Global Pty Ltd in May 2023; iTech Labs is a wholly owned subsidiary of GLI Australia Pty Ltd. Engaging both to obtain an independent second opinion does not achieve independence.
register.mitigation: Where a market or contract requires laboratory independence or a second-opinion certification, select from a different corporate group. Disclose the relationship to the client proactively.

register.title: B2B supplier is bound by operator licence conditions it has never seen
register.description: Operator licence conditions are generally not public but flow down contractually as technical requirements on the supplier. A supplier relying on GLI-19 conformity alone may miss market-specific obligations.
register.mitigation: Request a summary of applicable licence conditions from each operator partner. Agree an interface compliance responsibility matrix so no checkpoint is orphaned.

register.title: Hard external system dependency with no operational fallback
register.description: Known instances: German per-game GGL permission, German LUGAS and Limitdatei, Swedish Spelpaus API (Actor ID / API key from 2026-08-01), Danish SAFE and TamperToken, Ontario iGO centralised self-exclusion, Kahnawake single co-location facility. If the dependency is unavailable, lawful operation stops.
register.mitigation: Confirm fail-closed behaviour, define an availability incident procedure, and agree with the operator who communicates with the regulator during an outage. Note that fail-open is a compliance breach, not a workaround.

register.title: A feature is treated as a configuration flag when it is in fact a separate maths model
register.description: Jackpot removal (Germany) redistributes RTP. A different RTP target is a different paytable and reel strip. See steering/jurisdiction-matrix.md section 3.2.
register.mitigation: Classify each market difference as flag-able or model-affecting before committing to an architecture. Budget a separately verified maths model where required.

register.title: Static maximum stake configuration cannot express age or behavioural risk tiering
register.description: UK tiers stake caps by age (GBP 5 / GBP 2). Germany is expected to tier by age and by problem-gambling indicators in a rolling 90-day window, which makes max stake a runtime service dependency.
register.mitigation: Design maxStake as an interface resolvable at runtime from an external risk and player-attribute service, not as a static config value.

register.title: A target market prohibits online slots or has grey legal status
register.description: Confirmed prohibited: Australia, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, India, South Africa. Grey trending prohibited: Mexico. No regulator: Costa Rica. See templates/market-profiles/_prohibited-and-grey-markets.json.
register.mitigation: Technical compliance cannot resolve legal status. Remove the market from scope or obtain local legal advice. Note that Japan's 2025 amendment extends criminal exposure to marketing and affiliate activity.

register.title: Outcome determined by a non-cryptographic RNG or determinable on the client
register.description: Product cannot be certified in any market. Requires core logic rework.
register.mitigation: Escalate immediately, ahead of all other work. See steering/rng-game-logic.md and steering/platform-systems-compliance.md section 2.

register.title: Single retention strategy conflicts with a mandatory deletion duty
register.description: German GlueStV section 6h(5) requires deletion of parallel-play data after the waiting period and bans other uses, which conflicts with blanket long-term append-only retention.
register.mitigation: Classify audit data by category with separate retention and deletion rules. See steering/data-protection-privacy.md section 1.2.

register.title: Data residency requirement discovered after the deployment architecture is fixed
register.description: Confirmed hard requirements: Sweden (gaming system in Sweden), West Virginia (in-state data warehouse), Brazil (in-country data centres). Probable: Belgium, Romania, Portugal, Spain, Netherlands, New Jersey, Connecticut.
register.mitigation: Confirm data residency in phase 1 of market entry assessment, before architecture is committed.

register.title: Production build does not correspond to a valid certification report
register.description: Commonly caused by hotfixes bypassing the compliance gate, or by automatic dependency upgrades changing the build hash.
register.mitigation: Maintain a build-to-certification mapping table. Add a pre-deployment compliance gate. Pin dependency versions. See steering/change-management-recert.md.
